reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Transfer of duties, property, records, and obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1967 p. 357 § 14). Covers transferring all statutory duties and functions of the office of state and regional planning and community development to the department and the department's succession to all property, documents, records, assets, and obligations.

headings.title: Completion of pending matters by department
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1967 p. 357 § 14). Covers completion by the department of pending matters begun but not completed before the former office, qualified by 'insofar as practicable and desirable'.

headings.title: Transfer and continued availability of unencumbered balances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1967 p. 357 § 14). Covers the historical transfer of unencumbered balances of the former office to the department as of October 13, 1967, and their continued availability for the original purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (L. 1967 p. 357 § 14) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed succession of duties, property, records, and obligations (1), the "insofar as practicable and desirable" qualification for pending matters (2), and the historical October 13, 1967 unencumbered-balance transfer and continued availability (3). All 3 drafted titles retained as accurate and neutral.

headings.title: Definitions for sections 251.010 to 251.440
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (6) and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 § 7, A.L. 1967 p. 361 § 6, A.L. 1986 S.B. 426, A.L. 1993 H.B. 555). Defines 'director', 'governing body', 'local governmental units'/'local units', 'population', 'state office', and 'transportation planning boundary' (citing 23 U.S.C., section 134) strictly for sections 251.010 to 251.440.

headings.title: Petition, hearing, and gubernatorial creation of commissions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers permissive creation of a regional planning commission by gubernatorial order upon local governing body resolution petition, public hearing (or discretionary waiver if all local units including county commissions join), ten-day mailed notice to clerks, finding of need, consent of local units with over fifty percent of decennial census population, and boundary designation considering homogeneity elements.

headings.title: Referendum exemption and county zoning exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Exempts commission creation and local participation in or adoption of regional plans from a referendum notwithstanding section 64.530, while explicitly carving out county zoning laws or regulations under sections 64.620 to 64.690.

headings.title: Preservation and governance of preexisting planning organizations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Protects the legal existence, powers, and functions of previously constituted public or private comprehensive planning organizations (including federal transportation planning bodies) approved by local units with a majority of area population, and specifies that constituting resolutions, this section, or other applicable law govern them.

headings.title: Governor's concurrence for certain transportation boundary changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires gubernatorial concurrence to change a transportation planning boundary only for a regional planning commission acting as a metropolitan planning organization within an MSA over 500,000 population that does not contain a city not within a county.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–5 (including subdivisions 1(1)–(6)) and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 § 7 through A.L. 1993 H.B. 555) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked section-range scope (251.010 to 251.440) and 23 U.S.C. § 134 citation in (1), permissive gubernatorial creation and >50% population consent in (2), section 64.530 referendum exemption and 64.620–64.690 county zoning carve-out in (3), preexisting planning body preservation in (4), and the MSA >500,000 / non-independent-city MPO qualification in (5). All 5 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: State planning agency designation, contracting, delegation, and reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 § 4, A.L. 1967 p. 361 § 4, A.L. 1986 S.B. 426). Designates the office of administration as official state planning agency for requested local/regional assistance and authorizes contracting under 251.010–251.440, delegating functions (with responsibility remaining solely with 'the state office'), and actual-cost reimbursement unless covered by federal grants. Source discrepancy retained explicitly: official catchline refers to 'Department' while body designates 'the office of administration' and subdivision (2) refers to 'the state office' (defined in 251.160 as the department of economic development).

headings.title: Block-grant expenditure reporting, fund withholding, and cure period
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers the office of administration gathering block-grant matching expenditure data from assisted regional planning commissions, reporting eligible expenditures to the department of economic development within thirty days of determination, interagency information sharing, withholding next fiscal year's general revenue funds for noncompliance, and a thirty-day cure period for any regional planning authority prior to withholding. Independent review revised title to clarify general revenue fund withholding and noted the subsection's internal shift from "regional planning commission" to "regional planning authority" in the cure-period sentence.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 (including subdivisions 1(1)–(3)) and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 § 4 through A.L. 1986 S.B. 426) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Explicitly verified and retained without repair the agency-naming discrepancy (catchline says "Department", body (1) designates "the office of administration", and 1(2) retains responsibility with "the state office", defined in 251.160 as DED) as well as subsection 2's shift from "regional planning commission" to "regional planning authority". Retained title (1) and revised title (2) to specify "fund withholding" for general revenue funds.

headings.title: Transfer of comprehensive planning duties to state office
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 § 33). Transfers duties and functions of the division of commerce and industrial development relating specifically to state, regional, or local comprehensive planning to the state office.

headings.title: Succession to related property, records, assets, and obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers the state office's succession to property, documents, records, assets, and obligations of the division of commerce and industrial development necessary to the transferred planning duties and functions.

headings.title: Completion of pending matters under 251.150 to 251.440
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers state office completion of pending division matters under sections 251.150 to 251.440, qualified by 'insofar as practical and desirable'.

headings.title: Transfer and continued availability of planning section balances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers the historical transfer as of August 4, 1966, of unencumbered balances of the division's planning section allocated for duties under sections 251.150 to 251.440 to the state office and their continued availability for original purposes.

headings.title: Retention of division's community betterment program powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Preserves administration of the division's community betterment program and retains all planning powers necessary for the division to administer that program.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–5 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 § 33) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified limitation to comprehensive planning duties in (1), related-assets scope in (2), "insofar as practical and desirable" and 251.150–251.440 range in (3), historical August 4, 1966 transfer of planning-section balances in (4), and retention of community betterment program powers in (5). All 5 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Membership composition and county population calculation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 §§ 8, 9), and cross-reference note (Commission to include legislative members, 251.038). Covers determining commission membership composition via resolutions of local governing bodies representing at least half of the region's population, treating a county as one local unit based on unincorporated-area decennial census population.

headings.title: Member terms, elector status, and regional residency
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and cross-reference note to section 251.038. Sets member terms per the resolutions of approval and requires all members to be state electors residing within the region.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2, history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 §§ 8, 9), and cross-reference note (legislative members under 251.038), and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed majority-population resolution mechanism and county unincorporated-area census calculation in (1) and member terms, state-elector, and regional-residency requirements in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Plan filing, public hearing, notice, and adjournment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 §§ 17, 18). Covers pre-adoption/amendment/extension filing of the comprehensive plan or portion with the state office, holding at least one public hearing with fifteen days' newspaper, state-office, local-unit, and township-posting notices, and authority to adjourn the hearing from time to time.

headings.title: Amending, extending, adding to, or detailing the plan
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Grants permissive authority ('may') for the commission to amend, extend, add to, or carry parts of the comprehensive plan into greater detail using original-plan adoption procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 §§ 17, 18) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed state-office filing, fifteen-day publication/notice/township-posting rules, and adjournment authority in (1), and permissive amendment/extension/addition/detailing authority in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Referral of plan facility sites and land acquisitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 § 21). Requires the local officer or public body with final authority to refer the location of or land acquisition for items or facilities included in the adopted regional comprehensive plan to the commission for consideration and report.

headings.title: Commission report timing and advisory effect
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the commission to report recommendations within twenty days of referral or a longer period stipulated by the referring officer or body, and specifies that the report and recommendations are advisory only.

headings.title: Authorizing commission plat examination, review, or approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits local units and state agencies, with the commission's consent, to authorize the commission to act for them in approving, examining, or reviewing plats pursuant to sections 64.070, 64.245, 64.590, 64.820, 64.830, and 88.163. Independent review revised title to clarify permissive local-unit or state-agency authorization with commission consent rather than standing authority.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 908 § 21) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed mandatory local referral for adopted-plan facilities/land acquisitions in (1), twenty-day or stipulated-longer advisory report in (2), and permissive local-unit/state-agency authorization with commission consent under sections 64.070–64.830 and 88.163 in (3). Retained titles (1)–(2); revised title (3) to avoid implying standing commission plat authority.

headings.title: Program plan development, coordination, and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 1223 & 1246 § 5). Covers joint development of the Main Street program plan by the departments of economic development and natural resources with assistance from specified stakeholder organizations, and required plan descriptions of objectives, intergovernmental/private coordination, and city selection and assistance methods.

headings.title: Selection of ten pilot cities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the department to select ten pilot cities in which to initiate the program.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 1223 & 1246 § 5) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed joint DED/DNR plan development with stakeholder assistance and required contents in (1), and department selection of ten pilot cities in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Establishing an economic development district and its purpose
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 1201 § 2). Grants permissive authority for governing bodies of adjoining counties, or counties and a city not within a county, to establish an economic development district by identical ordinances or mutual agreement for economic development programs.

headings.title: Board membership, appointments, officers, and meeting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers ordinance/agreement determination of board qualifications, terms, and size subject to equal representation, resident appointments by county chief executive officers and city mayors plus one jointly appointed member, officer selection, and meeting at least four times a year.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 1201 § 2) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified permissive establishment by adjoining counties or county/counties and city not within a county in (1), and equal representation, resident appointments plus one joint appointee, officer selection, and quarterly meeting minimum in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Establishing a regional economic development district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741). Grants permissive authority for two or more governing bodies to establish a regional economic development district by identical ordinances or mutual agreement to plan, develop, promote, fund, or conduct economic development programs.

headings.title: Board composition, appointments, officers, and open meetings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers determination of board qualifications, terms, and size subject to equal representation, appointment of one resident per governing body by county CEO or city mayor plus one jointly appointed member, selection of chairman, treasurer, and other officers, and open-session meetings to set policy and administer activities.

headings.title: Public governmental body status and chapter 610 compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Designates the regional economic development district as a public governmental body for section 610.010 and requires compliance with chapter 610.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed permissive creation by two or more governing bodies in (1), equal representation, resident appointments plus joint member, treasurer selection, and open-session meetings in (2), and section 610.010 / chapter 610 status in (3). All 3 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Sales tax authorization, rates, and voter submission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741). Covers eligible entire cities/counties forming a regional economic development district imposing by resolution a retail sales tax under chapter 144 (sections 144.010 to 144.525) at 1/8%, 1/4%, 3/8%, or 1/2%, conditioned on submission to voters at a general, primary, or special election, in addition to and stated separately from other taxes.

headings.title: Ballot form and voter approval or rejection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including the ballot table and the continuation paragraph, and history note. Sets substantial ballot form (with YES/NO boxes and voting instructions) and states the legal effect of majority approval versus majority opposition and resubmission.

headings.title: Collection cost and sales tax trust fund creation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs deposit of collected sales taxes, less one percent for collection cost (to state general revenue after section 32.087 surety bond premiums), into the newly created Regional Economic Development District Sales Tax Trust Fund.

headings.title: Non-state fund status and public inspection of records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Specifies that trust fund moneys are not state funds and may not be commingled with state funds, and requires the director of revenue to keep per-city/county collection records open to inspection by the district board, local governing body, and public.

headings.title: Monthly revenue distribution and expenditure compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires monthly distribution by the tenth day of each month from the director of revenue to the levying city or county treasurer for the district's benefit, with all expenditures complying with the regional economic development district law.

headings.title: Refunds for overpayments and dishonored check redemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Grants permissive authority to the director of revenue to authorize state treasurer refunds from credited trust fund amounts for erroneous payments or overpayments and to redeem dishonored checks and drafts.

headings.title: Abolition notice, one-year retention, and account closure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Distinguished from subsections 9 and 13 by governing post-abolition administration: ninety-day prior notice to director of revenue, optional one-year two-percent retention for refunds/dishonored checks, remittance of balance and account closure after one year, and notice to the city or county of each refund or redeemed check.

headings.title: Applicability of sections 32.085 and 32.087
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Applies all provisions of sections 32.085 and 32.087 to taxes imposed under this section, qualified by 'except as modified in and by this section'.

headings.title: Dedicated use, post-repeal funds, and local investment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Requires deposit into a special trust fund solely for designated purposes, continues that restriction for remaining funds after repeal, and permits city or county investment of unneeded funds under applicable local investment laws.

headings.title: Board hearings, thirty-day vote, and expenditure authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Requires the board to consider plans, projects, or designations, hold noticed public hearings, vote on proposals and amendments within thirty days after hearing completion, and make the final determination on use and expenditure of tax funds.

headings.title: Exclusion from special taxing districts and approval exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Excludes this sales tax from revenues available to special taxing districts (such as TIF, NID, or CID districts) and bars using its revenues for those districts unless approved by both the district board and the imposing city or county governing body.

headings.title: Annual report on fund use and project progress
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note. Requires the district board to report at least annually on fund use and progress of adopted plans, projects, or area designations, available to the public and the imposing city or county governing body.

headings.title: Restrictions on repeal or amendment and repeal petitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Bars repeal or amendment if it would impair repayment of district liabilities, borrowings, or obligations, and requires submission of a repeal proposal upon petition by ten percent of qualified voters (subject to the same non-impairment condition), with majority-vote effect.

headings.title: Severability of regional economic development district law
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and history note. Declares the provisions and applications of the regional economic development district law severable if any part or application is held invalid.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–14 (including the ballot table and continuation paragraph in subsection 2 and subdivisions 13(1)–(2)) and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified voter-submission prerequisite and entire-city/county scope in (1), ballot form plus continuation-paragraph approval/rejection and resubmission rules in (2), 1% collection cost and trust fund creation in (3), non-state status and records in (4), monthly distribution in (5), permissive refunds/check redemption in (6), post-abolition 90-day notice/1-year 2% retention/closure in (7), qualified 32.085/32.087 applicability in (8), dedicated use and investment in (9), hearings/30-day vote/expenditure finality in (10), special taxing district exclusion with dual-approval exception in (11), annual reporting in (12), non-impairment restrictions and 10% voter repeal petitions in (13), and severability in (14). All 14 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Incremental tax financing, retail exclusion, and allocation fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741). Permits a district board, after adopting a regional economic development plan, to adopt incremental tax financing by resolution, excludes all retail projects from incremental tax financing, and requires the treasurer to establish a special allocation fund upon the first resolution. Independent review revised title to specify the special allocation fund and retail exclusion.

headings.title: County assessor certification of initial assessed value
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the county assessor upon resolution adoption to sum the most recently ascertained equalized assessed value of taxable real property in the project area and certify that total in writing to the board treasurer as total initial equalized assessed value (noting the source text refers to both 'regional economic development district' and 'regional economic development project area').

headings.title: Division of property taxes, PILOTs, and excluded levies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note. Covers the twenty-five calendar year (unless earlier terminated) division of ad valorem taxes and PILOTs at section 251.627 rates: (1) initial EAV plus annual CPI-U adjustment to affected taxing districts; (2) incremental PILOTs into a segregated special allocation fund account as a foreclosable lien, excluded from the section 163.031 school aid formula until expiration or termination; and (3) exclusion of blind pension fund tax (Mo. Const. Art. III, § 38(b)), merchants'/manufacturers' inventory replacement tax (Art. X, § 6, subsec. 2), desegregation sales tax, and conservation taxes.

headings.title: Allocation of fifty percent of economic activity taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 3 (property taxes/PILOTs) by allocating fifty percent of economic activity taxes from the project area for twenty-five calendar years (unless earlier terminated) into a separate segregated account within the special allocation fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 (including subdivisions 3(1)–(3)) and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed post-plan permissive TIF adoption, retail-project bar, and special allocation fund establishment in (1), county assessor EAV certification (retaining the source's district vs. project-area wording) in (2), 25-year tax/PILOT division with CPI-U adjustment, school-aid exclusion under 163.031, and excluded constitutional/local levies in (3), and 25-year 50% economic activity tax allocation in (4). Revised title (1) to name the allocation fund and retail exclusion clearly; retained titles (2)–(4).

headings.title: Required contents of regional economic development plan
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (15) and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741). Sets a non-exhaustive list of fifteen required written plan elements, from chairman contact details, site location, estimated costs, funding sources/commitments/terms, and EAV estimates to land uses, benefits, prior/sought subsidies, public investments, market study, and board accuracy certification.

headings.title: Required findings, analyses, and limits for plan adoption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (5) and history note. Covers permissive adoption in reliance on reasonable-person findings regarding lack of private growth, twenty-five-year completion/retirement and fifteen-year project-approval time limits, cost-benefit analysis including school districts, prohibition on gambling establishment development/redevelopment, and economic feasibility analysis with pro forma ROI statement capped at reimbursable project costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 (including subdivisions 1(1)–(15) and 2(1)–(5)) and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed non-exhaustive 15-item plan contents in (1) and permissive adoption in reliance on reasonable-person findings, 25-year/15-year time limits, cost-benefit analysis, gambling-establishment bar, and ROI feasibility analysis capped at reimbursable costs in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Terminating incremental tax financing and distributing surplus funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741). Requires a termination resolution once all project costs and financing obligations are paid in full, resumes normal tax levies, and specifies distinct distribution rules for surplus PILOTs, surplus economic activity taxes, and other remaining special allocation fund moneys.

headings.title: Dissolving special allocation fund and area designation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by requiring a subsequent resolution dissolving the special allocation fund and terminating the regional economic development area designation after costs are paid, obligations retired, and surplus funds distributed.

headings.title: Constitutional uniform tax rate requirement preserved
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Clarifies that nothing in the regional economic development district law relieves property in such areas from paying a uniform tax rate under Article X, Section 3 of the Missouri Constitution.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified full-payment termination resolution, tax resumption, and distinct surplus distribution rules (PILOTs, EATs, other funds) in (1), subsequent dissolution of the special allocation fund and area designation in (2), and preservation of Mo. Const. Art. X, § 3 uniform tax rates in (3). All 3 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Authorization, terms, security, and sale of revenue bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741). Permits a district to authorize and issue revenue bonds (up to twenty-five-year maturity) by resolution to pay project costs, secured by district revenues and property, with flexible bond forms, rates, redemption terms notwithstanding section 108.170, and public or private sale.

headings.title: Refunding outstanding district bonds and amount limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes issuing refunding bonds at any time up to principal, unpaid interest, premiums, commissions, service fees, and refunding expenses, whether matured or unmatured, by sale or holder-consented exchange across same or separate projects.

headings.title: Limited district obligation and required bond disclaimer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Restricts bond liability solely to pledged district funds and property (not a debt of the state or any agency or political subdivision) and requires an express disclaimer on the face of the bonds.

headings.title: State tax exemption for bonds, interest, and proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Exempts bonds issued under this section, interest thereon, and any proceeds from taxation in Missouri (noting the official catchline mentions only interest, while the body covers bonds, interest, and proceeds).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 and history note (L. 2007 H.B. 741) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified permissive revenue bond issuance (<=25-year maturity, notwithstanding 108.170) in (1), refunding bond caps and exchange consent in (2), exclusive district liability and face disclaimer in (3), and state tax exemption covering bonds, interest, and proceeds (broader than the catchline's reference to interest only) in (4). All 4 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Interagency meetings and coordination for energy grants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 1181, et al.). Requires representatives of five specified state departments to meet at least twice per calendar year to collaborate on securing Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 (Pub. L. 110-140) or similar green-energy grants, and designates the department of natural resources as coordinating agency.

headings.title: External consultation and partnerships for securing grants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Grants permissive authority ('may') for listed departments to confer with or invite participation by external individuals, nonprofits, private entities, higher education institutions, or local governments and enter partnerships in accordance with federal grant requirements and other law.

headings.title: Annual joint report to general assembly and governor
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the five departments in subsection 1 to submit a joint annual report on grant-securing actions to the general assembly and governor by the first Wednesday after the first Monday of January.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 1181, et al.) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed twice-yearly meetings of five named departments and DNR coordination for Pub. L. 110-140/green-energy grants in (1), permissive external consultation and partnerships in (2), and joint annual report deadline to the general assembly and governor in (3). All 3 drafted titles retained.
